newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep. Gonzalez faces challenge to banking spot.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep. Gonzalez faces challenge to banking spot.

text.p: Congressman Henry Gonzalez faces challenges from other House Banking Committee members for his position as the ranking Democrat on the committee, Congressional aides said Monday.

House Democrats are expected to vote Wednesday to choose committee leaders. Gonzalez, D-Texas, held the ranking spot in the past Congress after being Banking Committee chairman from 1989 to 1994 when the Democrats controlled the House.
The two challengers are Rep. Bruce Vento, D-Minn., and Rep. John LaFalce, D-NY, Congressional aides said.
Current House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach, R-Iowa, was not expected to be challenged for that position.

Gonzalez has sent letters to Democrats seeking their support, saying he wants just another two years as the ranking committee member and then, if re-elected, would be willing to act in an "emeritus" manner.
Gonzalez wrote a letter to House Minority Leader Richard Gephardt, D-MO, after the two met Friday, in which Gonzalez said he believed he had been "subjected to unfair attack."
Gonzalez added: "It is not my purpose or intent to be divisive, but I do have an obligation to defend my record."

"On the basis of that record, my desire to serve a final term with a clear goal of transition to an emeritus role is fair, reasonable and one that I hope you will support," Gonzalez wrote in his letter to Gephardt.
The challengers cited Gonzalez's absences at committee hearings during the past Congress.

"Most of the time over the last two years, I have had to assume the responsibilities of Ranking Democrat at full committee hearings and markups...," LaFalce wrote in a letter to House Democrats advising of his intention to seek the ranking Democrat spot on the Banking Committee.
In a letter on Monday to Democratic colleagues, Congressional Black Caucus Chairman Donald Payne, D-NJ, and Hispanic Caucus Chairman Ed Pastor, D-Az, expressed their support for Gonzalez.
The letter said Gonzalez was successful in resisting Republican efforts to dismantle housing programs, consumer protection and bank safety laws in the last Congress.
